guard: the mesh handler's liveness pair is real: `down` is the death of ONE incarnation read off presence (name AND lifecycle uid), the reason distinguishes a lapsed name from a superseded one, the timeout is one absolute deadline that arms, expires, is attached to on re-entry, and is claimed on every ending, and `monitor` validates the registration it journals, and `monitor` is the prerequisite: the registration binds the handle, `wait(down)` refuses an agent nobody monitored, and an adopted run rebuilds the registry from settled monitor entries
why: Lane F durable-actions step 5 (2026-09-02): `monitor` + `wait(down)` leave the not-yet-durable
seam and perform over presence liveness. Each half of the contract has a mutant: the
incarnation pin in the liveness match (MM1), the death check itself (MM2), the two reasons
(MM3), the expiry observation (MM4), the timer claimed on a down (MM5), the arm that makes the
deadline exist at all (MM6), monitor's validation of the handle it registers (MM7), and the
routing that sends a down descriptor to this machinery instead of the channel path (MM8).
All eight mutate mesh-handler.ts, which the suite imports through a relative `../src` path —
no build sits between the mutation and the run.
Batch B1 (2026-09-03) makes monitor the prerequisite the reference states (6.5): the
registry, the wait's gate on it, and its adoption-time seed each have a mutant.
